blocks.h2_above: How Do You Create Your First Interactive Map with leaflet?
blocks.prose_above: Every leaflet map starts with three steps: call leaflet(), add a tile layer for the basemap, and set a view centre. The result is a live, zoomable map you can embed in R Markdown, Shiny apps, or stand...
blocks.code:
library(leaflet)

m <- leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  setView(lng = -0.1276, lat = 51.5074, zoom = 13)
m
#> A leaflet map widget centred on London
#> - Pan by clicking and dragging
#> - Zoom with scroll wheel or +/- buttons
#> - OpenStreetMap tiles load automatically

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: This is the most common legend problem. You set a colour directly, then wonder why no legend appears. ❌ Wrong:
blocks.code:

  geom_point(colour = "red", size = 2)
# No legend appears — colour is not mapped to data.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: Why it is wrong: ggplot2 only creates legends for aesthetics mapped inside aes(). Setting colour = "red" applies a fixed colour to all points with no data mapping. ✅ Correct:
blocks.code:
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 2)
# Legend appears because colour is mapped to the class variable.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: When your plot has both a colour and a size legend, theme(legend.position = "none") removes both. ❌ Wrong:
blocks.code:
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class, size = cty)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
# Both colour AND size legends are gone.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: Why it is wrong: legend.position = "none" is a blanket removal. It does not discriminate between aesthetics. ✅ Correct:
blocks.code:
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class, size = cty)) +
  geom_point() +
  guides(size = "none")
# Only size legend is removed. Colour legend remains.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: labs() sets the legend title, not the individual labels. Using it and expecting label changes leads to confusion. ❌ Wrong:
blocks.code:
p_base +
  labs(colour = c("2-Seater", "Compact", "Midsize"))
# This does NOT rename individual labels.
# It may produce an error or unexpected title.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: Why it is wrong: labs() expects a single string for the title. Pass a named vector to scalecolourdiscrete(labels = ...) instead. ✅ Correct:
blocks.code:
p_base +
  labs(colour = "Vehicle Class") +
  scale_colour_discrete(
    labels = c("2seater" = "2-Seater", "compact" = "Compact",
               "midsize" = "Midsize")
  )
# Title is "Vehicle Class", and three labels are renamed.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: Changing the order of scalecolourdiscrete(limits = ...) reorders the legend but does not reassign colours. The safest approach is to relevel the factor in the data. ❌ Wrong:
blocks.code:
p_base +
  scale_colour_discrete(limits = c("suv", "pickup"))
# Only suv and pickup appear in the legend.
# All other classes are dropped from the legend AND the plot.

blocks.h2_above: Common Mistakes and How to Fix Them
blocks.prose_above: Why it is wrong: limits restricts the scale to the values you list. Any value not in limits is treated as NA and removed. ✅ Correct:

  levels = c("suv", "pickup", "minivan", "midsize",
             "compact", "subcompact", "2seater"))

ggplot(mpg_fixed, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5)
# All classes are present, but legend order starts with SUV.
